hypothesis: Among one-dimensional nearest-neighbour cellular automata, exactly 6 of the 256 two-colour rules and exactly 1800 of the 3^27 = 7,625,597,484,987 three-colour rules are reversible, where reversible means the global map on bi-infinite configurations is injective (equivalently bijective; equivalently, by Wolfram's note, all periodic configurations have distinct successors).
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. An exhaustive enumeration with an exact injectivity test (pair graph of the de Bruijn graph: a rule is injective iff the pair graph has no cycle through an off-diagonal node and no diagonal-to-diagonal path through off-diagonal nodes; used both as a sound pruning condition during depth-first assignment of the rule table and as the exact test at the leaves) yields exactly 6 reversible rules for k = 2, r = 1 and exactly 1800 for k = 3, r = 1. As a check of the method, the same program must give 62 for k = 2, r = 2 (NKS note 'Numbers of reversible rules'), and the 6 elementary rules must be {15, 51, 85, 170, 204, 240}. Also, every rule found must pass Wolfram's finite test (distinct successors for all periodic configurations of period <= 9, as his note says suffices for k = 3) and every rule not found that is sampled (10000 random balanced k = 3 rules) must fail it. 'Supports' requires the counts 6 and 1800 and the consistency checks.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'Refutes' if the exhaustive enumeration completes and gives a count other than 6 for k = 2, r = 1 or other than 1800 for k = 3, r = 1 (with the k = 2, r = 2 check giving 62, so the method is validated). If the k = 3 enumeration cannot be completed within the compute budget (about 1 hour), the verdict is 'mixed' or 'inconclusive' (reason: other) with the k = 2 result and a lower bound on the k = 3 count reported.
interpretation: 'Reversible' is taken as injectivity of the global map on the full shift (bi-infinite configurations), the standard notion and the one Wolfram's note tests through periodic configurations. Rule numbering is Wolfram's (table entry for neighbourhood (l,c,r) at digit position l*k^2 + c*k + r of the base-k rule number). The count is of raw rule tables, not of symmetry classes (the note gives 172 families for k = 3). The enumeration is exact, so there is no sampling uncertainty; the only risks are implementation errors, which the k = 2 (r = 1 and r = 2) checks and the independent periodic-configuration test guard against. Note: the pruning search is written in C (compiled with gcc from analysis.py) because a Python search over the pruned tree would be too slow; this is a deviation from 'python3 only' tooling and is recorded.

datasets.name: Exhaustive enumeration of nearest-neighbour cellular automaton rules (generated by analysis.py + revca.c)
datasets.version: analysis.py and revca.c in this directory

generator.script: analysis.py (compiles and runs revca.c with gcc)
generator.program_family: all k^(k^3) one-dimensional CA rules with k colours and radius 1 (k = 2, 3), and k = 2 radius 2 as a method check
generator.initial_conditions: not applicable (injectivity is a property of the rule)
generator.steps: depth-first assignment of rule-table entries ordered by the period of their neighbourhood word, pruning with the pair-graph criterion and the balance condition (each colour exactly k^(2r) times in a surjective rule)

datasets.role: the enumerated program family and the list of reversible rules found (derived/)

datasets.name: NKS notes 'Numbers of reversible rules' and 'Testing for reversibility' (p. 1017)
datasets.role: the reversibility test Wolfram used (ReversibleQ) and the stated counts 6, 62, 1800 used as the method check
